title.narrative: Emergency Response to the Returnees in Fashoda County - Kodok

description.narrative: Upper Nile State sharing the largest border with Sudan is receiving the biggest number of the people fleeing the conflict in Sudan through the border entry point at Joda, north of Renk town. People have been entering Upper Nile State in tens of thousands from the onset of the conflict until today. The International Organization for Migration (IOM) in partnership with the Government provided transport to tens of thousands of people. The Catholic diocese of Malakal, through its Caritas Office, provided transport to about 5,000 people mostly from Upper Nile State. Short term humanitarian support to returnees that are settling in the transit camps or temporary camps in the State, particularly in Malakal town and Kodok (Fashoda County), has been and remains a great challenge given their high numbers and given the long duration of this emergency situation. Caritas Malakal has received multiple appeals from a number of locations, but this appeal focuses on the temporary camp for returnees in Kodok (Fashoda County). To date, 16,489 individuals have settled in Kodok, with most of them still hosted at a temporary camp opened by the local Government in the southern part of the town. The conditions of most of the returnees are of high vulnerability. Their main needs are food, Shelter NFIs and Clean water, according to the Chairperson of the Relief and Rehabilitation Commission of Fashoda County. This project will look at the following priority interventions: • Deliver life-saving assistance to most vulnerable people among the returnees from Sudan (Multi-purpose cash). • Deliver essential shelter NFIs to most vulnerable people among the returnees from Sudan (tarpaulins). • Carry out hygiene and sanitation messaging to promote good hygiene and practice. • Carry out peace messaging to promote peaceful coexistence/social cohesion.
